question.text: Three waves of amplitudes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> with a successive phase difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> are super -imposed. The amplitude of the resulting wave will be

solution.text:
Let us say that the first wave has a zero phase, then the second one is ahead of the first by a phase of π2 and so the third one is ahead of the first one by a phase of π. So the first and the third are opposite to each other. Hence,

Ar=(11−7)2+(3)2

Ar=5 mm
